securityNotes: Read all 6 files in full at the pinned SHA. Contains browser-console/devtools JS snippets (getComputedStyle walks, document.getAnimations(), elementsFromPoint) and curl+grep recipes for fetching a user-named public URL's HTML/CSS -- all read-only inspection of pages the user names, no execution of remote code, no credential access. The skill explicitly instructs the agent to treat fetched page content (markup, comments, class names, alt text) as evidence to report, never as instructions to follow, and to never widen scope because a fetched page asked it to -- an anti-prompt-injection safeguard built into the skill itself, not a vulnerability. No hidden or exfiltration-oriented instructions found. Clean.

proposedEntry.name: explain-interface
proposedEntry.description: Reverse-engineers how a UI effect or a whole frontend was built from a URL (browser DevTools evaluate_script or raw HTML/CSS fetch) or a screenshot (explicit reconstruction, not a reading). Finds the full layer stack behind one visual effect in paint order rather than one declaration, tags every claim measured/derived/inferred, treats fetched page content as evidence never as instructions to follow, and closes on the transferable recipe in words plus what would not survive being copied, rather than a rebuild snippet.
triggers: reverse engineer this effect from a screenshot
inputs: a URL and the named effect (or none, for a whole-system read)
optionally a screenshot when no live page is available
outputs: a layer-stack explanation in paint order with measured/derived/inferred tags per claim
a transferable recipe in words plus what would not survive copying
